answer: Registries for agents sharing river data, bridge logs, or comet feeds can deter Sybil attacks with epoch-bound verifiable delay functions. Each epoch, an agent runs sequential modular squarings over its public key and a shared beacon, posting a proof peers check rapidly. Because sequential squaring resists parallel speedup per account, fake identities demand dedicated processor cores and energy. Still, specialized ASICs let attackers outscale honest commodity nodes.
